concepts.title: Terminal, Shell และการเดินทางในระบบไฟล์ (pwd, ls, cd)
concepts.covers: Explain OS/kernel/shell/terminal briefly, then how to read the prompt `somchai@DESKTOP-K7Q2M4P:~$` ($ = normal user, # = root). Teach pwd; ls with -l -a -h -t; cd with ~ .. - and /; absolute vs relative paths; . and ..; hidden dotfiles (.bashrc, .profile, .bash_logout); the main FHS folders (/, /home/somchai, /root, /etc, /var/log, /usr/bin, /usr/local, /tmp, /opt, /dev, /proc) and /mnt/c as the Windows C: drive in WSL; Tab completion; history, !! and Ctrl+R; case sensitivity; names with spaces. CODE EXAMPLE (deterministic, real output): `mkdir -p ~/projects/linux-lab/c01/{docs,images,'my notes'}` then a navigation session: cd ~ && pwd; cd projects/linux-lab/c01 (relative) && pwd; cd /home/somchai/projects/linux-lab/c01/docs (absolute) && pwd; cd .. && pwd; cd - ; cd "my notes" && pwd; ls -la ~/projects/linux-lab/c01; plus `ls /` with a note that WSL also shows entries such as init, snap, lost+found and *.usr-is-merged that a container may not have. Mistakes rows: `bash: cd: Documents: No such file or directory` (wrong case), `bash: cd: my: No such file or directory` (unquoted space), `bash: cd: /etc/hostname: Not a directory`.

concepts.title: จัดการไฟล์และโฟลเดอร์ด้วย touch, mkdir, cp, mv, rm และ Wildcards
concepts.covers: touch; mkdir and mkdir -p; rmdir; cp, cp -r, cp -i, cp -v; mv to move and rename, mv -i; rm, rm -i, rm -r, why rm -rf is dangerous (no trash) and the habit of running ls with the same glob before rm; globbing * ? [0-9] [abc]; brace expansion {a,b} and {001..005} and how it differs from globbing; file and stat; ln -s; good file naming (lowercase, no spaces, ISO dates). CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c02, a small 'shop' folder: mkdir -p shop/{orders,reports,archive}; touch shop/orders/order-{001..005}.txt; touch shop/reports/sales-2026-10-{17,18,19}.csv; ls shop/orders/order-00[1-3].txt; cp -v shop/reports/*.csv shop/archive/; mv -v shop/orders/order-005.txt shop/orders/order-005-cancelled.txt; touch shop/tmp-{1..3}.tmp then ls shop/*.tmp then rm -v shop/*.tmp; tree shop (tree 2.1.1 installed in the Part 2 setup). Show real output. Mistakes rows: `cp: -r not specified; omitting directory 'shop/orders'`, `rm: cannot remove 'shop/orders': Is a directory`, `rmdir: failed to remove 'shop/orders': Directory not empty`, `mv: cannot stat 'order-9.txt': No such file or directory`.

concepts.title: ดูเนื้อหาไฟล์ แก้ไขด้วย nano และหาความช่วยเหลือ (cat, less, head, tail, man)
concepts.covers: cat and cat -n; less navigation (Space, arrows, /search, n, g, G, q); head -n and tail -n; tail -f for live logs (stop with Ctrl+C); wc -l -w -c; nano 7.2 keys (Ctrl+O then Enter to save, Ctrl+X exit, Ctrl+W search, Ctrl+K cut line, Ctrl+U paste, Ctrl+G help); Vim survival (i, Esc, :w, :wq, :q!, vimtutor); export EDITOR=nano; help sources: man ls (man sections 1, 5, 8), --help, help cd for builtins, type, which, whatis, apropos / man -k, tldr 0.9.2 (first run downloads pages, tldr --update). CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c03: create server-notes.txt with a heredoc of 12 numbered lines (e.g. 'line 01 boot ok' ... or short server notes), then cat -n server-notes.txt | head -n 5; head -n 3; tail -n 3; wc -l -w -c server-notes.txt; a live-log demo: `( for i in 1 2 3; do echo "event $i" >> app.log; sleep 1; done ) &` then `timeout 5 tail -f app.log`; then `type cd`, `type -a ls`, `whatis ls`, `ls --help | head -n 3`. Note that in an interactive WSL shell `type ls` shows the alias `ls --color=auto`. Mistakes rows: stuck inside Vim (Esc then :q!), `E37: No write since last change (add ! to override)`, nano 'Save modified buffer?' prompt, `No manual entry for xyz`, man saying the system is minimized (fix: sudo unminimize, only if that message appears).

concepts.title: Permissions, Ownership, Users และ sudo (chmod, chown, umask)
concepts.covers: Reading ls -l (type, rwx for user/group/others, owner, group); r/w/x meaning on files vs directories; chmod numeric (755, 644, 700, 600, 750) and symbolic (u+x, g-w, o-r, a+r); chown/chgrp with sudo; umask (somchai on Ubuntu usually 0002 giving 664/775; some setups show 0022; tell the learner to check with `umask`); users and groups: id, groups, /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /etc/shadow (root only); sudo adduser, sudo groupadd, sudo usermod -aG, sudo deluser --remove-home, su - user; sudo vs root, sudo -l, visudo; sticky bit on /tmp (drwxrwxrwt) and setuid on /usr/bin/passwd (-rwsr-xr-x); /mnt/c files show rwxrwxrwx. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c04: create hello.sh (echo "Hello from somchai"), ls -l, ./hello.sh -> `bash: ./hello.sh: Permission denied`, chmod u+x hello.sh, run it; echo 'API_TOKEN=fake-123' > secret.txt; chmod 600 secret.txt; stat -c '%A %a %U:%G %n' hello.sh secret.txt; umask; id; then sudo groupadd developers; sudo adduser --disabled-password --gecos "" labuser; sudo usermod -aG developers labuser; id labuser; sudo -u labuser cat secret.txt -> Permission denied; sudo deluser --remove-home labuser; sudo groupdel developers. Realistic `id` for somchai on WSL: uid=1000(somchai) gid=1000(somchai) groups=1000(somchai),4(adm),20(dialout),24(cdrom),25(floppy),27(sudo),29(audio),30(dip),44(video),46(plugdev),100(users) (say the list may differ). adduser 3.137ubuntu1 on 24.04 also adds new users to group users(100). Mistakes rows: Permission denied on ./script, `chmod: changing permissions of 'x': Operation not permitted` (not owner), `usermod -G` without -a wiping groups, `sudo: unable to resolve host` is NOT needed; prefer `somchai is not in the sudoers file.`

concepts.title: จัดการแพ็กเกจด้วย apt (update, install, remove, search)
concepts.covers: Packages, repositories, dependencies; /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (deb822 format on 24.04); apt update vs apt upgrade vs full-upgrade; apt search, apt show, apt policy; sudo apt install -y; remove vs purge vs autoremove; apt list --installed / --upgradable; dpkg -l, dpkg -L, dpkg -S; apt vs apt-get (apt-get in scripts; the warning `WARNING: apt does not have a stable CLI interface. Use with caution in scripts.` when apt output is piped); Snap/PPA/.deb risks; common errors. CODE EXAMPLE using cowsay (apt version 3.03+dfsg2-8 on noble): sudo apt update; apt policy cowsay; apt show cowsay 2>/dev/null | head -n 5; sudo apt install -y cowsay; cowsay "Hello somchai" (binary is /usr/games/cowsay; /usr/games is in the normal WSL user PATH, in the root sandbox call /usr/games/cowsay and mention it); dpkg -L cowsay | grep bin; dpkg -S /usr/games/cowsay; sudo apt purge -y cowsay; sudo apt autoremove -y. Show real output from the sandbox (trim long apt progress output and say it was trimmed). Mistakes rows: `E: Unable to locate package cowsy`, `E: Could not open lock file /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend - open (13: Permission denied)` (forgot sudo), `E: Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend. It is held by process 1234 (apt)`, `cowsay: command not found` (PATH/games).

concepts.title: Pipes และ Redirection (>, >>, 2>, 2>&1, tee, /dev/null)
concepts.covers: stdin(0)/stdout(1)/stderr(2); > overwrite, >> append, < input, 2> errors, 2>&1 merge (and why order matters: `> file 2>&1` vs `2>&1 > file`), &> Bash shortcut, /dev/null, | pipe, tee and tee -a, here-strings briefly. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c06 using members.csv (canonical sample below): ls /etc/hostname /nope > out.txt 2> err.txt; cat out.txt; cat err.txt (real error `ls: cannot access '/nope': No such file or directory`); ls /etc/hostname /nope > all.txt 2>&1; echo "run 1" > run.log; echo "run 2" >> run.log; cat run.log; find /etc -name '*.conf' 2>/dev/null | wc -l (number varies -> note); tail -n +2 members.csv | sort -t, -k4 -nr | head -n 3 | tee top3.txt; sort < members.csv | head -n 2. Real output. Mistakes rows: file emptied by `sort data.txt > data.txt`, errors still on screen because only > was used, `bash: out.txt: cannot overwrite existing file` when set -o noclobber, `tee: /etc/x: Permission denied` (use sudo tee).

concepts.title: Text Processing: grep, find, sort, uniq, cut, tr, sed, awk และ xargs
concepts.covers: grep -i -n -v -c -r -l -w -o -E with basic regex (^ $ . * + ? [0-9] (a|b)); sort -n -r -k -t -u -h; uniq -c -d (sort first); cut -d -f; tr (case, -d, -s); sed s///g, /pattern/d, -n '2,4p', -i.bak; awk '{print $1}', -F',', NR>1, filters, sum/avg in END (awk on Ubuntu 24.04 is mawk 1.3.4, write POSIX awk); find -name -iname -type -size -mtime -exec {} \; -delete (test first); xargs and -print0 | xargs -0. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c07 with the canonical access.log (10 lines) and members.csv: top 3 IPs `awk '{print $1}' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 3` (real output: '      4 192.0.2.10' / '      3 203.0.113.5' / '      2 198.51.100.23'); `grep -c '" 404 ' access.log` -> 3; `grep -E '" (404|500) ' access.log | awk '{print $1, $7, $9}'`; status counts `awk '{print $9}' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` (real: 5 200, 3 404, 1 500, 1 302); cities `tail -n +2 members.csv | cut -d, -f3 | sort | uniq -c`; average score `awk -F, 'NR>1 {s+=$4; n++} END {printf "avg=%.2f\n", s/n}' members.csv`; uppercase names with tr; `sed 's/Bangkok/BKK/' members.csv`; then `touch a.tmp b.tmp 'c d.tmp'` and `find . -name '*.tmp' -print0 | xargs -0 rm -v`. Real output.

concepts.title: Environment Variables, PATH, ~/.bashrc และ alias
concepts.covers: Shell variable vs environment variable (export), env/printenv, $HOME $USER $SHELL $PWD $LANG, ${VAR:-default}; how PATH lookup works left to right, which, type -a, `command not found`; ~/.local/bin (Ubuntu ~/.profile adds it to PATH when it exists at login) or export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"; ~/.bashrc vs ~/.profile vs /etc/environment; source; alias/unalias and functions (mkcd); HISTCONTROL, HISTTIMEFORMAT, PS1; WSL interop: code ., explorer.exe ., clip.exe, wslpath -w, Windows PATH appended (/mnt/c/Windows/system32 and others); CRLF problem `$'\r': command not found`; secrets belong in env vars/.env + .gitignore. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c08: demo `CITY=Bangkok; bash -c 'echo "child sees: ${CITY:-<empty>}"'` then `export CITY` and run again; `echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | head -n 5`; create ~/.local/bin/sysinfo (file block: #!/usr/bin/env bash; prints user, host, kernel via uname -r, date +%F), chmod +x, export PATH, `which sysinfo`, run it; append alias lab and function mkcd to ~/.bashrc with a heredoc (>>), `source ~/.bashrc`. For WSL-only commands (wslpath -w ~/projects -> `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-24.04\home\somchai\projects`, explorer.exe ., clip.exe) state they cannot run in a plain Linux sandbox and show predicted output with a note. Note: sourcing ~/.bashrc in a non-interactive shell returns early on Ubuntu (the `case $- in *i*` guard); test with `bash -i -c` in the sandbox.

concepts.title: Processes, Signals และ Job Control (ps, top, kill, jobs, nohup)
concepts.covers: Process, PID, PPID, process states; ps aux, ps -ef, ps -o pid,ppid,stat,etime,cmd; pgrep -a, pkill; top keys (P, M, q) and htop 3.3.0 (F3 search, F9 kill, F6 sort); signals SIGINT 2, SIGTERM 15 (default), SIGKILL 9 (last resort, cannot be trapped), SIGHUP 1, SIGTSTP (Ctrl+Z), kill -l; jobs, &, fg %1, bg %1, Ctrl+Z, nohup, disown; trap in scripts for graceful shutdown; free -h, uptime/load average, nproc, /proc/loadavg; tmux 3.4 mention. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c09: file worker.sh (#!/usr/bin/env bash, set -euo pipefail, trap 'echo "$(date +%T) ได้รับสัญญาณ TERM กำลังปิดอย่างปลอดภัย"; exit 0' TERM; trap ... INT; loop writing a heartbeat line to worker.log every second); run `nohup ./worker.sh > worker.out 2>&1 &`, `echo "PID=$!"`, `sleep 3`, `ps -o pid,ppid,stat,cmd -p <pid>`, `pgrep -af worker.sh`, `kill <pid>` (SIGTERM), `sleep 1`, `tail -n 3 worker.log`; plus a jobs demo `sleep 300 &` `sleep 400 &` `jobs` `kill %1 %2`. PIDs and times vary -> note. Mistakes rows: `kill: (12345) - No such process`, `bash: kill: %1: no such job`, using kill -9 first (no cleanup, temp files left), process dies when terminal closes (use nohup/tmux), `-bash: fg: current: no such job`.

concepts.title: Services ด้วย systemd: systemctl, journalctl และ Log ใน /var/log
concepts.covers: systemd as PID 1; WSL: /etc/wsl.conf [boot] systemd=true, check with `ps -p 1 -o comm=` (systemd vs init), wsl --shutdown after editing; units and .service files; systemctl status/start/stop/restart/reload/enable/disable/is-active/is-enabled/--failed/list-units --type=service --state=running/daemon-reload; journalctl -u, -f, -n, --since "10 min ago", -p err, -b, --no-pager; /var/log (apt/history.log, dpkg.log, syslog and auth.log only if rsyslog is installed), dmesg; fallback `sudo service cron status/start` without systemd. CODE EXAMPLE: (1) check PID 1 and cat /etc/wsl.conf; (2) manage cron: systemctl status cron --no-pager, sudo systemctl stop cron, systemctl is-active cron, sudo systemctl start cron, systemctl is-enabled cron, journalctl -u cron -n 5 --no-pager; (3) own service: folder ~/projects/linux-lab/c10/site with index.html, unit file /etc/systemd/system/hello-web.service (Description, After=network.target, User=somchai, WorkingDirectory=/home/somchai/projects/linux-lab/c10/site, ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080, Restart=on-failure, WantedBy=multi-user.target), then sudo systemctl daemon-reload, sudo systemctl enable --now hello-web, systemctl status hello-web --no-pager, curl -s localhost:8080, journalctl -u hello-web -n 5 --no-pager, sudo systemctl disable --now hello-web. The sandbox has no systemd as PID 1 (systemctl prints the real errors `System has not been booted with systemd as init system (PID 1). Can't operate.` and `Failed to connect to bus: Host is down`): show realistic systemctl/journalctl output and say clearly that dates, PIDs, memory and CPU values differ. You CAN show real output for `curl` by running the python server manually, and for `sudo service cron start/status` (real: ` * Starting periodic command scheduler cron` / `   ...done.` / ` * cron is running`).

concepts.title: Networking พื้นฐานและ SSH Keys (ip, ss, curl, dig, ssh-keygen)
concepts.covers: IP, port, DNS, localhost; ip -br a, ip a, ip route, hostname -I, ping -c 3, curl -I / -s / -o, wget, ss -tulpn (sudo to see other users' process names), dig, dig +short, nslookup (bind9-dnsutils 9.18), /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf (generated by WSL, often nameserver 10.255.255.254 with DNS tunneling; values vary); WSL2 NAT (eth0 typically 172.x.x.x/20, differs from Windows IP), localhost forwarding to Windows browser, mirrored mode (networkingMode=mirrored in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig on Windows 11); SSH: openssh-server 9.6p1, Ubuntu 24.04 socket activation (ssh.socket), ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "somchai@wsl", passphrase, ssh-copy-id, authorized_keys, permissions 700 ~/.ssh and 600 private key/config, ssh-agent/ssh-add, ~/.ssh/config Host alias, scp, rsync -avz; hardening (PasswordAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin no). SAFETY: practise only on localhost/own machines; mention พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์; never share the private key. CODE EXAMPLE in ~/projects/linux-lab/c11: python3 -m http.server 8000 in background + curl -sI http://localhost:8000/ | head -n 1 (real: `HTTP/1.0 200 OK`) + ss -tln | grep 8000 (real: `LISTEN 0      5            0.0.0.0:8000       0.0.0.0:*`) + kill %1; ping -c 3 127.0.0.1; then SSH to localhost: sudo apt install -y openssh-server; ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "somchai@wsl" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_lab; ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_lab.pub somchai@localhost; file block ~/.ssh/config (Host lab / HostName localhost / User somchai / IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_lab / IdentitiesOnly yes); chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config; ssh lab 'whoami; hostname'. In the sandbox you can start sshd with `service ssh start` (or /usr/sbin/sshd) to get real output; fingerprints, randomart, IPs and hostnames vary -> note.

concepts.title: Bash Scripting ที่เชื่อถือได้ และตั้งเวลาด้วย cron
concepts.covers: Shebang #!/usr/bin/env bash; set -euo pipefail; variables and quoting; $(...) and $(( )); ${var:-default} and ${var:?msg}; arguments $0 $1 $# "$@"; if/[[ ]] tests (-d -f -z -n -eq -gt), case; for and while read -r loops; functions with local; exit codes and $?; stderr with >&2; trap ... EXIT; readonly; date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S; ShellCheck 0.9.0 (SC2086 demo); bash -x debugging; disk & archives (tar -czf / -tzf / -xzf -C, df -h, du -sh); cron: crontab -e / -l, 5-field syntax, absolute paths, `>> log 2>&1`, escape % as \%, cron PATH is minimal, cron service must run in WSL and WSL must be open, verify with journalctl -u cron or grep CRON /var/log/syslog; installing a line non-interactively with `(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "...") | crontab -`. CODE EXAMPLE: file ~/projects/linux-lab/c12/backup.sh: usage `backup.sh <source_dir> [keep]` (keep default 5), BACKUP_DIR="$HOME/backups", log() helper printing `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] msg`, validates arg count and -d, creates "$BACKUP_DIR/<name>-<timestamp>.tar.gz" with tar -czf -C parent dir, keeps only newest N archives (ls -1t ... | tail -n +$((keep+1)) | while read -r old; do rm -- "$old"; done), prints final archive size with du -h, exit 1 on bad input and 2 on usage. Sample data: ~/projects/linux-lab/c12/data/{notes.txt,members.csv,todo.txt}. Run: chmod +x; shellcheck backup.sh && echo 'shellcheck ผ่าน'; ./backup.sh ~/projects/linux-lab/c12/data 3 (run 4 times with sleep 1 to show rotation); ls -1 ~/backups; tar -tzf on newest archive; ./backup.sh /nope; echo $?; then the crontab line `0 2 * * * /home/somchai/projects/linux-lab/c12/backup.sh /home/somchai/projects/linux-lab/c12/data 7 >> /home/somchai/projects/linux-lab/c12/backup-cron.log 2>&1` and crontab -l. Timestamps vary -> note. Keep this distinct from the Part 4 health monitor (this one is a backup tool).

mini_project.name: Server Health Monitor
mini_project.summary: A portfolio-ready Bash tool for Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2) that measures CPU usage, RAM usage, Disk usage and load average, compares them with thresholds from a config file, appends one key=value line per run to a log file, returns Nagios-style exit codes, runs every 5 minutes with cron, rotates its own logs daily with a user-level logrotate config (no root needed), includes a report script that summarises the log with awk, and a test script; every script passes ShellCheck and the repo is pushed to GitHub. Project root: /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor (git repo, branch main). Final structure: server-health-monitor/ -> bin/health-check.sh (main script), bin/health-report.sh (summary), config/health.conf (thresholds), logrotate/health-monitor.conf (user-level logrotate config), cron/crontab.txt (the two cron lines to install), logs/.gitkeep (logs/health.log, logs/cron.log, logs/logrotate.state are created at runtime and git-ignored), tests/run-tests.sh, .gitignore (logs/*.log, logs/*.gz, logs/logrotate.state, logs/*.log-*), README.md.
mini_project.features: 1) Metrics: CPU % from two samples of the first line of /proc/stat taken 1 second apart (fields user nice system idle iowait irq softirq steal; idle_all = idle + iowait; usage = 100 * (dTotal - dIdle) / dTotal, integer); RAM % = 100 * (MemTotal - MemAvailable) / MemTotal from /proc/meminfo; Disk % from `df -P "$DISK_PATH" | awk 'NR==2 {gsub("%","",$5); print $5}'`; load1 from the first field of /proc/loadavg. Use only Bash integer arithmetic and POSIX awk (mawk 1.3.4 is the default awk). 2) Config file config/health.conf sourced by the script: CPU_WARN=70 CPU_CRIT=90 MEM_WARN=75 MEM_CRIT=90 DISK_WARN=80 DISK_CRIT=90 DISK_PATH=/ LOG_FILE="$HOME/projects/server-health-monitor/logs/health.log"; the script validates that thresholds are integers. 3) Status per metric and overall: OK / WARN / CRIT (worst wins). 4) Log line format (one line per run, appended): `2026-10-19T14:05:01+0700 host=DESKTOP-K7Q2M4P status=OK cpu=12 mem=41 disk=23 load1=0.15` using `date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'` and `hostname`. 5) Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 WARN, 2 CRIT, 3 UNKNOWN (bad option, missing/invalid config). 6) Options with getopts: -c FILE (config path, default <project>/config/health.conf resolved from the script's own location via `$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)`), -q quiet (log only, no stdout), -h help. 7) set -euo pipefail, functions (read_cpu, read_mem, read_disk, read_load, classify, write_log, main), messages to stderr with >&2, `flock -n` on logs/.lock (util-linux 2.39.3) so overlapping cron runs exit 3 with a message. 8) bin/health-report.sh [logfile]: awk summary of the log: number of checks, count per status, average and max of cpu/mem/disk, first and last timestamp. 9) cron/crontab.txt: `*/5 * * * * /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/bin/health-check.sh -q >> /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/logs/cron.log 2>&1` and `5 0 * * * /usr/sbin/logrotate -s /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/logs/logrotate.state /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/logrotate/health-monitor.conf` installed with `crontab cron/crontab.txt` (warn that this replaces the existing crontab; back up first with `crontab -l > ~/crontab-backup.txt`). 10) logrotate/health-monitor.conf (tested in the sandbox as a non-root user with logrotate 3.21.0, works with -s state file): `/home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/logs/health.log {` daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, dateext, create 0640 `}`; test with `logrotate -d -s logs/logrotate.state logrotate/health-monitor.conf` (dry run) and `logrotate -f -v -s ...` (force; real verbose output includes lines like `rotating log /home/somchai/projects/server-health-monitor/logs/health.log, log->rotateCount is 7`, `dateext suffix '-20261019'`, `renaming ... to ...health.log-20261019`, `creating new ... mode = 0640`). chmod 644 the config. 11) tests/run-tests.sh: runs shellcheck on all bin/*.sh and tests/*.sh; runs health-check with the normal config and checks the exit code is 0, 1 or 2 and the last log line matches a regex like `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T.* status=(OK|WARN|CRIT) cpu=[0-9]+ mem=[0-9]+ disk=[0-9]+ load1=`; runs with a temp config whose *_WARN/*_CRIT are 0 and expects exit 2 (CRIT); runs with a missing config and expects exit 3; runs health-report.sh and checks it prints the 'checks' line; prints PASS/FAIL per test and exits non-zero on any failure. Uses mktemp and trap cleanup. 12) Verification step shows real output of tests/run-tests.sh, a few health.log lines, health-report.sh output, crontab -l, and cron evidence (journalctl -u cron on WSL with systemd, realistic output flagged as varying; in the sandbox you can `service cron start` and wait for a real run). 13) README template: title, one-line description, features, requirements (Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 or any systemd Linux, bash 5.2, cron, logrotate), install steps, usage with options and exit-code table, sample log line, cron setup, log rotation, testing, WSL notes (cron only runs while WSL is running; check `ps -p 1 -o comm=`), skills shown (Bash, Automation, Linux Admin), license MIT. 14) Push to GitHub: git init -b main, git add, git commit, create repo server-health-monitor, git remote add origin git@github.com:<username>/server-health-monitor.git, git push -u origin main (link topic 17 for SSH keys/details). 15) Extension ideas: send alerts to a Discord/LINE webhook read from an env var (mock mode when the variable is missing), add network check with ping/curl, CSV export, systemd timer version instead of cron, HTML report, per-process top-3 CPU list in WARN/CRIT lines, run inside a Docker container (topic 12).
